keepouts.name: cell-body-HEIGHT-0.578mm
keepouts.why: DOCUMENTATION, NOT AN ENFORCED RULE, and the distinction is the point. A Ø20.0 mm CR2032 sits 0.578 mm below this face (ce-designs/halo/design.py (lane M): Z_CELL_TOP 4.022, Z_DECK_TOP 4.600). What is forbidden here is HEIGHT, not presence: a 0201 at 0.33 mm is welcome and a QFN-48 at 0.85 mm is not. KiCad rule areas have no height axis, so forbidding footprints outright would fail every part on the bottom face including the ones that fit - an alarm that is always on tells you nothing. The real check is arithmetic and it is in height_check() below, which grades each part against the allowance at its own radius.
keepouts.verdict_reason: the region forbids nothing, so no item could violate it and nothing was measured; a keep-out that forbids nothing is not a passing keep-out

keepouts.name: bender-diaphragm-HEIGHT-0.400mm
keepouts.why: DOCUMENTATION, same reason as the cell. The Murata 7BB-20-3 is bonded to the shell's Ø21.2 mm land and needs a 0.680 mm moving gap, so ce-designs/halo/design.py (lane M) limits top-face parts inside this circle to 0.400 mm. Height again, not presence: 0201 (0.33 mm) passes and every active on this board does not. Graded in height_check().
keepouts.verdict_reason: the region forbids nothing, so no item could violate it and nothing was measured; a keep-out that forbids nothing is not a passing keep-out

keepouts.name: antenna-host-clearance
keepouts.why: SPEC.md §4, Apple's own callout: no metal above or below, Ø37.31 mm - 11.44 mm LARGER than this board. Every square millimetre of halo is inside it, so it is a constraint on the HOST, and this board cannot grade it.
keepouts.note: host-scope: this region constrains whatever the board is fitted INTO, and 523.660 mm2 of the board's 523.660 mm2 lies inside it, so it cannot be graded from this file. Not enforced as a KiCad rule area either — it would fail every pad on the board for a rule that does not govern it.

keepouts.name: antenna-ground-clearance
keepouts.why: No ground plane, no inner copper and no bottom copper under the 2.4 GHz element. An inverted-F over its own ground plane is a short circuit. F.Cu is deliberately NOT in this list - the antenna itself lives there.
keepouts.note: host-scope: this region constrains whatever the board is fitted INTO, and 57.089 mm2 of the board's 523.660 mm2 lies inside it, so it cannot be graded from this file. Not enforced as a KiCad rule area either — it would fail every pad on the board for a rule that does not govern it.

keepouts.name: nfc-coil-clearance
keepouts.why: No plane copper and no vias within 0.30 mm of the NFC winding, on any layer. A 13.56 MHz loop with a solid plane one dielectric away is loaded by the eddy currents it induces in it; 74% of this coil's ring had ground on In1 and VDD on In2 until this existed. TRACKS are allowed because the winding itself is one, and because the two tie stubs and the coil's own escape have to cross this band.

keepouts.name: antenna-arm-shadow
keepouts.why: NOTHING under the 2.4 GHz arm on any layer the arm is not on. R10.8920 to R12.5000 is the arm's own copper grown by the 0.30 mm gap lane T3 solved as the working point; the same coil under the arm moves the resonance 668 MHz and no tuning recovers it. The element is on F.Cu only, so this forbids everything on the other three layers and still cannot forbid the element.
